Guenther & Son’s Recalled Biscuits. No Illnesses, Use-By Dates Through November 18, and Still No Public Notice From the Biscuit Maker. 
 USDA Issues Listeria Alert for Mmm! Meals Made In Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy Sold in Vending Machines in Six States, the Second Product Pulled Over C.H. Guenther & Son’s Recalled Biscuits. No Illnesses, Use-By Dates Through November 18, and Still No Public Notice From the Biscuit Maker.
 By Bill Marler on November 16, 2026 
 Posted in Food Poisoning Information 
 USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service issued a public health alert on November 14, 2026 for Mmm! Meals Made In Minutes brand Biscuit & Sausage Gravy, a 9.5-ounce ready-to-eat meal with use-by dates of November 12 through November 18, 2026, stocked mainly in vending machines in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas, because the biscuits in it were recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son of San Antonio for possible  Listeria monocytogenes  contamination. No illnesses have been reported. It is the second product pulled over the same biscuits in a week, after a Washington company recalled 2,414 biscuit sandwiches on November 7.
 FSIS issued an alert, not a recall, because the meals were already sold. 
 FSIS uses a public health alert when it is concerned that product is in consumers’ hands but a recall cannot be requested, usually because the product is no longer available for sale. According to the alert as reported by  Food Safety News , the problem surfaced when a federally inspected company told FSIS it had received FDA-regulated biscuits that C.H. Guenther & Son had recalled for possible  Listeria monocytogenes . The meat and gravy are USDA’s; the biscuit is FDA’s. FSIS says additional downstream products may be added as the ingredient recall investigation continues, so this list may grow. The agency’s own  alert page  was not loading this morning; the product details here come from Food Safety News, Shreveport’s KTAL and eFoodAlert’s roundup of the alert, and I will update when FSIS’s page and product list are reachable.
 Two products in eight states have now been pulled over one biscuit recall. 
 On November 7, Fresh & Ready Foods of Renton, Washington, recalled 2,414 Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwiches, 4.6 ounces, SKU 3100048, UPC 8 405493 0168 4, Fresh Thru dates 11/07 through 11/19, delivered to employee break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias in Washington and Oregon between October 25 and November 4, for the same reason: biscuits recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son. I wrote that recall up  here . Fresh & Ready is the company whose San Fernando, California sandwiches were linked to a 2025  Listeria  outbreak that hospitalized ten people and killed one.
 Date Company Product and codes Where Agency 
 Nov 7 Fresh & Ready Foods, Renton WA Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich, 4.6 oz, SKU 3100048, UPC 8 405493 0168 4, Fresh Thru 11/07–11/19; 2,414 units WA, OR break rooms, vending, cafeterias FDA recall notice 
 Nov 14 Not named in available reporting Mmm! Meals Made In Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy, 9.5 oz, use-by 11/12/26–11/18/26 AR, LA, MS, OK, TN, TX vending machines FSIS public health alert 
 Sources: FDA recall notice of November 8, 2026 (Fresh & Ready) and the FSIS alert of November 14, 2026 as reported by Food Safety News, KTAL and eFoodAlert, read November 16. Check: 2 states + 6 states = 8 states; two downstream products, one biscuit supplier. 
 The biscuit recall itself still has no public notice. 
 C.H. Guenther & Son is a large San Antonio baker whose brands include Pioneer, White Wings and Morrison’s. Its biscuit recall has not appeared on  FDA’s recall page , which as of this morning is current to November 13, and the company’s website carries no statement. Nine days after the first downstream recall, the public still does not know which biscuits were recalled, what lots, what dates, where they went, or whether any were sold at retail under the company’s own brands rather than baked into someone else’s product. Both companies that did go public are the ones that bought the biscuits. The one that made them has not. I raised the same point when the Washington sandwiches were recalled and in the  November 14 Weekend Wrap-Up .
 Listeria  symptoms can take up to 70 days to appear, and pregnant women face the most danger. 
 Listeria monocytogenes  is unusual among food bacteria because it grows at refrigerator temperatures and because illness can begin anywhere from a few days to 70 days after eating contaminated food, with most invasive cases starting within one to four weeks. In healthy adults it usually causes a short illness with fever and diarrhea that is rarely diagnosed. In pregnant women it may feel like a mild flu but can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery or a life-threatening infection in the newborn. In adults over 65 and people with weakened immune systems it can cause invasive infection, with fever, muscle aches, headache, stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance or convulsions. About one in five people with invasive listeriosis dies.
 If you ate one of these products, watch for symptoms and tell your doctor about the  Listeria exposure. 
 Check break-room and home freezers and vending purchases for the products above and throw them out or return them. If you ate one and are pregnant, over 65 or immunocompromised, call your doctor now even if you feel well, because a blood test and preventive treatment are available. Anyone who develops fever and muscle aches, especially with headache, stiff neck or confusion, in the next two months should seek care and say they may have been exposed to  Listeria , since the diagnosis requires a blood or spinal fluid culture that doctors do not order unless they are told. The USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline is 888-674-6854.
 Three questions people are asking. 
 I bought a biscuit and gravy meal from a vending machine at work. How do I know if it is the one?  Look for the Mmm! Meals Made In Minutes name, a 9.5-ounce package and a use-by date between November 12 and November 18, 2026. If the package is gone and you are not sure, treat it as exposed and watch for symptoms.
 Nobody has gotten sick. Why is this an alert?   Listeria  illness can take up to 70 days to show up, so a product sold November 12 cannot be called safe on November 16. The alert is issued because the biscuit supplier found or was told of a  Listeria  risk, not because a patient has been matched to it yet.
 Were the biscuits sold on their own in stores?  Nobody has said. The biscuit maker has not published a recall notice, and FDA has not posted one. If that changes, this post will be updated.
